instagram_caption:
Who bets their own house on a movie? 🎬

Francis Ford Coppola did. Making Apocalypse Now in the Philippines (1976-77), Newsweek reported he put up all his own assets as guarantees on the loans, while a typhoon and a year-long shoot pushed costs far past the original twelve million dollars.

The film won the top prize at Cannes in 1979, so the bet paid off.

Decades later he did it again. Megalopolis reportedly cost about 120 million dollars, and he funded it himself after selling part of his wine business.

The quiet part: that wine business began with Godfather profits. A film paid for the vines, and the vines paid for a film.
